title: acp-stack /v1 API and configuration contract
description: Generated from the Rust wire types of acp-stack; do not edit by hand — regenerate with `cargo run --features dev-tools --bin generate-api-schema`. This root is a container of definitions, not a validatable body: validate a payload against `#/$defs/<namespace>/<TypeName>`. `$defs` splits into three namespaces because serde's `default` and `skip_serializing_if` attributes place a field in `required` under one direction but not the other — `request` is the deserialize contract (what a client sends), `response` is the serialize contract (what the server emits), and `config` is the deserialize contract for `acps-config.toml`. A type used on both sides appears once per namespace. Conventions: timestamp fields are RFC 3339 strings; an optional response field is omitted when absent rather than emitted as null, so its nullable type means absent and null are equivalent. Not covered, by design: the `/v1/ws` `LiveEvent` frames and the `acps init serve` streaming frames and state signals (hand-built and byte-pinned by golden tests), the envelope-bypassing binary download handler and the `health/ready` handler (whose readiness body is hand-built, not a typed DTO), and the untyped `config` import response. Cross-field rules (mutually-required or mutually-exclusive fields, exactly-one-of constraints, blank-as-absent) are mostly inexpressible in JSON Schema and stay enforced in code; `ApiError.code` is likewise an open dotted-namespace string rather than a closed enum. See docs/specs/api/api.md for both.

DesiredState.description:
The desired payload, discriminated by `kind`. A second kind later is an
additive change; unknown kinds fail deserialization.

values.description: Inline values keyed by env-var name.

source_refs.description:
Secret-store refs keyed by env-var name; each resolves into `values`
at apply time and the ref name is retained alongside the value.

base_url.description:
Endpoint base the agent must send this provider's traffic to instead of
the vendor default. Written into the agent's own native config, so the
configured agent must declare `set_provider_base_url` in the registry.

limit.description: Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.

confirmation.description:
Operator must set `confirmation = true` for the apply to run.
Mirrors the CLI's `--yes` flag; without it the endpoint returns
a structured preview without spawning any subprocess.

feature.description:
Optional `feature` filter — only deps whose `feature` matches
are eligible. `None` means apply every actionable dep.

reason.description:
Recorded as `operator_reason` on each `ws.client_disconnected` event.
Omitted here means the event carries no `operator_reason` field.

Recorded as `operator_reason` on each `ws.client_disconnected` event.
Omitted here means the event carries no `operator_reason` field.

active.description: When true, only in-flight (`running`) rows are returned, oldest first.

agent.description:
Scope to one agent id (`deps_apply` covers dependency installs);
absent returns rows for every agent.

limit.description: Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.
Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.
Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.
Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.
Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.
Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.

since.description:
Window start. Accepts RFC3339 (e.g. `2026-05-16T00:00:00Z`) or a
duration suffix (`1h`, `30m`, `2d`). Defaults to 24h ago.

until.description: Window end. Same format as `since`. Defaults to "now".

target_id.description:
Array target id to discover against instead of the default
(primary) target.

limit.description:
Defaults to 20 when omitted. Values above 500 are silently clamped to
500, not rejected.

command.description:
Command name as advertised (no leading slash required; one is
stripped if present).

args.description: Optional free-form arguments appended after the command name.

config_id.description: The advertised option id to set.

value.description:
The value to apply: a string for select options, a boolean for
boolean options.

SessionConfigOptionSetValue.description: `Bool` first so JSON `true` never deserializes as the string `"true"`.

limit.description: Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.
Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000, not rejected.

prompt.description:
Either a bare string, which becomes a single text block, or an array of
ACP content blocks (camelCase, e.g. `[{"type":"text","text":"..."}]`)
deserialized element-wise. `null`, an empty array, and any other JSON
type are rejected.

source.description: Catalog alias, configured user alias, or `github:<owner>[/<repo>]`.
Catalog alias, a configured user alias, or `github:<owner>[/<repo>]`.

skills.description: Skill selectors; comma-separated values in an entry are also accepted.

skill.description:
Install name of the skill to remove (a `/`-joined path for nested
skills, e.g. `zoom/android`).

custom_agent_id.description:
Escape-hatch agent declared inline, mirroring the `--custom-agent-*`
flags: its prompts are never streamed, so the whole spec must arrive
here. Requires non-blank `custom_agent_command` and
`custom_agent_install`; conflicts with `agent`, `provider`, `model`,
`mode`, `effort`, and `custom_provider: true`. Every other
`custom_agent_*` field requires it.

mode.description:
Declared up front like `model`, so a hosted client that already knows
the session mode it wants skips the streamed picker entirely. Validated
against the agent's advertised modes by the shared mode lane.

effort.description:
Declared up front like `mode`. Validated against the agent's
ACP-advertised reasoning-effort values (the `thought_level` session
config option) by the shared effort lane.

custom_provider.description:
Requires `provider`. Gates the custom-provider fields below
(`provider_name`, `base_url`, `provider_api`, `model_name`, `context`,
`output_max_tokens`), each of which requires `custom_provider: true`.

sandbox.description: Sandbox isolation backend for the agent workload.

deps_apply_async.description:
Requires `deps_apply`. Runs the confirmed install in a detached
background worker; the deps step settles as `background` and the run
is polled via `GET /v1/deps/apply/runs/{apply_run_id}`.

stack_update.description:
Stack self-update policy, declared up-front rather than streamed,
mirroring `--stack-update`. Absent leaves the `[updates.acp_stack]`
schema default.

agent_update.description:
Agent auto-update policy, mirroring `--agent-update`; honored only for
managed registry agents. Absent leaves the `[agent.auto_update]` default.

defer_provider_credentials.description:
The caller's declaration that it will push the configured provider's
credential through the managed-state extension after init. Only then does
a missing provider ref soft-pass, and only for a ref the push can deliver:
a custom provider's api-key ref, or a mapped key-based provider's api-key
and companion env vars under the names the agent reads. A noncanonical
api-key alias, a `VAR=template` inner ref, or an agent-native-auth
provider's refs cannot arrive through the push and still hard-fail.
Absent → false.

extensions.description:
`[extensions]` tables staged into a freshly-created starter config,
e.g. `{ "network-egress": { "type": "network-provider", "provider": [...] } }`.
Semantic validation (name shape, per-type field discipline, the
network-provider/unshare pairing) runs in-session with the rest of the
config validation. Applies only when creating a starter config.

sandbox_mask_paths.description:
Absolute paths unioned into the starter config's
`[workspace.sandbox].mask_paths`, so a network-provider declared through
`extensions` has its egress config/state dirs masked from the first
sandboxed spawn. Applies only when creating a starter config.

resume.description:
Continue the most recent unfinished or failed run instead of starting a
new one, matching `--resume`. Conflicts with `fresh`.

fresh.description: Force a new run, matching `--fresh`. Conflicts with `resume`.

env.description:
A bare secret-ref name exported under that name, or a `VAR=template`
entry whose template interpolates `${SECRET_REF}` (see config.md).

McpHttpHeaderRequest.description:
Exactly one of `value_ref` (whole-value secret ref) or `value`
(`${NAME}`-interpolated template) must be set; enforced in
`into_init_args` so a malformed declaration is a 400 at the boundary.

ExtensionConfig.description:
A typed, data-declared extension seam. An `[extensions.<name>]` table
declares one instance of an acp-stack-defined extension type; acp-stack
supervises or serves the type's generic contract and never learns the
extension's semantics. The struct is flat across all types; the extensions
validator rejects fields that do not belong to the declared `type`.

provider.description:
`network-provider` only. Lifecycle provider argv, invoked as
`<exe> setup|teardown <args...>` around each network-isolated spawn.
Empty means no provider: the namespace stays deny-all.

provider_timeout.description:
`network-provider` only. Duration string applied independently to
provider setup and teardown.

provider_stderr.description:
`network-provider` only. Where provider stderr goes: the daemon's
stderr diagnostic channel, or discarded. Stdout is always discarded.

workload_env.description:
`network-provider` only. Environment variables injected into every
workload spawned inside the provider's namespace (agent harness,
mediated commands, ACP terminals) so the workload can reach whatever
egress path the provider set up — proxy endpoints, CA bundle paths.
Never passed to the provider executable itself, and never in argv.
`BTreeMap` for deterministic ordering across serialization round-trips.

capability.description:
`managed-state` only. The state contract the namespace applies;
`provider-credential` is the only capability today.

ExtensionType.description:
The extension types acp-stack defines. Declaring a `network-provider`
instance switches every sandboxed spawn to an isolated network namespace
whose policy belongs to the external provider executable; declaring a
`managed-state` instance grants an external orchestrator ownership of a
named state namespace via the admin apply endpoint.

deferred.description:
Sibling of `value` on an `input` frame: the answer is `false` because
the hosting backend will run the confirmed work itself later, not
because the operator declined. Only the testflight confirm reads it.

value.description: Missing means JSON null, matching the frame's `value.unwrap_or(Null)`.

deferred.description:
Sibling of `value`, meaningful only to the testflight confirm; see
`ClientFrame::deferred`.

SessionInputRequest.description:
REST twin of the WebSocket `input` client frame (see `ClientFrame` in
routes.rs): same fields, defaults, and answer semantics. Unknown fields are
ignored to match the frame's forward-compat handling, so a client may POST a
socket frame verbatim (including its `type` discriminator) or carry fields a
newer backend adds, rather than hitting a 422 the socket would not.

DepositCredentialRequest.description:
Bootstrap-tier credential deposit (`POST /v1/init/credential`): flat-store
secrets plus a managed credential apply, mirroring the admin-tier
managed-state apply body (`POST /v1/admin/extensions/{name}/apply`) with
the namespace carried in the body instead of the path. Secret values are
opaque to acp-stack and stored verbatim.

secrets.description:
Flat-store secrets written before the managed apply resolves, so a
`source_refs` entry may reference a name this same body deposits.

namespace.description:
Managed-state extension namespace the apply targets; must resolve to a
declared `type = "managed-state"` instance in the runtime config.

apply.description:
The admin-tier apply body, verbatim: schema version, revision, and the
kind-discriminated desired state.

DepositSecretEntry.description:
One flat-store secret in a deposit. The value rides the bootstrap token's
channel rather than the prompt stream because the hosting platform cannot
answer a secret-ref prompt with a value it holds sealed.

ok.description:
Always `true` on a success envelope; the discriminator against
[`ApiErrorEnvelope`], whose `ok` is always `false`.

Always `false` on an error envelope; the discriminator against
[`ApiSuccess`], whose `ok` is always `true`.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable error identifier. An open, versioned set of
dotted `<domain>.<condition>` strings (e.g. `config.invalid`,
`request.invalid_param`, `agent.inference_5xx`). Not a closed enum —
clients match known values and treat unknown codes as generic
failures. See docs/specs/api/api.md and docs/specs/state-logging.md.

capabilities.description:
Raw ACP `initialize` capability JSON, surfaced verbatim. Always a JSON
object; its inner shape is the agent's, not ours.

AgentConfigOptionsResponse.description:
`GET /v1/agent/config-options`: every session config option the configured
agent advertises on a provisional `session/new`, projected verbatim —
including `model_config`, `_`-prefixed customs, and category-less options
the typed `/v1/models` lanes do not carry. Discovery failure is a hard
error: unlike `/v1/models` there is no catalog to fall back to, and an
empty list would be indistinguishable from "advertises nothing".

options.description:
Select choices, flattened across groups (group headers dropped) so
this list never disagrees with the codec's value matching. Absent for
boolean options.

SessionConfigOptionSnapshot.description:
One advertised config option, as served over the API and stored in the
per-session snapshot. `_meta` is deliberately dropped (agent-opaque and
unbounded); the verbatim `session.update` events remain the source of
truth for full payloads.

SessionConfigOptionSnapshotValue.description:
`Bool` first so JSON `true` never deserializes as the string `"true"`;
mirrors `AgentConfigOptionValue`'s ordering constraint.

prior_exit_status.description:
Exit status of the prior process. `None` when the supervisor
was not running (the restart degenerated into a plain start).

capabilities.description:
Raw JSON object of the agent's advertised capabilities. We surface it
verbatim so clients can read every field today without the daemon
growing a struct for each one. Named accessors land alongside the
session API.

agent_name.description:
`agentInfo.name` if the agent provided it. The spec says `SHOULD`,
not `MUST`, so this is best-effort.

AgentCapabilitiesDto.description:
Our owned view of the `initialize` response. Mirrors the protocol shape
but is independent of the SDK's `AgentCapabilities` type so our
`GET /v1/agent/capabilities` JSON contract stays stable across SDK
minor-version churn.

install.description:
Absent on resumed/no-op retries: install is a pre-commit step that the
interrupted attempt already ran, and re-running it on every retry
would re-burn minutes for no state change.

value.description: Model id accepted verbatim by `acps agent set --model`.

kept_unmanaged.description:
Same-named target skills left untouched because they carry no managed
marker — user-owned content is never replaced.

errors.description:
Per-skill failures (`"<skill>: <error>"`) that were skipped so the
rest of the refresh could continue; empty when every skill linked.

oneOf.description: Installed and upstream agree on a non-empty version.
Both versions are known and they differ — operator should re-run install.

We could not derive an upstream version (shell-recipe install, missing
registry kind, or upstream API error captured as a fall-through).
No successful installer row for this step yet.

AgentUpdateStatusComponent.description:
Result of comparing the installed managed-agent version against upstream.
Carried as a typed enum so the CLI printer, the API route, and test cases
can pattern-match the four states deterministically.

provider_error.description:
Set when this target's provider resolution fails; other targets keep
reporting so one broken credential never aborts the whole fleet status.

applied.description:
True when subprocesses ran. False on a preview call
(`confirmation = false`); the operator sees the candidate list
without any side effects.

candidates.description:
One-line summaries of every candidate action, including
scope=system warnings.

report.description: Full apply report when `applied = true`. `None` on preview.

post_status.description:
Status of the dep's `creates` binary AFTER the action ran.
`available = true` confirms the action actually installed the
thing it claimed to install.

oneOf.description: Action ran and the `creates` postcheck resolved.

`creates` already resolved before the action ran; the action
was skipped entirely. Mirrors the agent installer's
"already_present" semantics.

Action declared `scope = "system"` but the process isn't root
and passwordless sudo is unavailable. No subprocess was spawned.

Action ran but `creates` did not resolve afterwards, OR the
action exited non-zero. Tail of stderr included for context.

origin.description:
Surface that started the apply: `init`, `init_background`, `cli`, or
`api`.

live.description:
Whether the owning process is alive right now; meaningful while
`status = "running"`.

retryable.description:
True for terminal non-success states a re-`POST /v1/deps/apply` can
retry (the apply is idempotent over already-installed deps).

actions.description:
Per-action `installer_runs` rows sharing this apply_run_id, oldest
first. Step metadata only, never captured log contents.

DepsApplyRunDetailResponse.description:
One `deps_apply_runs` row for the polling surface. `running` rows are
reconciled against process liveness before serialization, so a crashed
apply reads as `failed` + `retryable` here rather than `running` forever.

elapsed_seconds.description:
Seconds since `started_at`, computed server-side so pollers need no
clock sync with the daemon; present only while the row is `running`.

origin.description:
Surface that started the apply: `init`, `init_background`, `cli`, or
`api`.

live.description:
Whether the owning process is alive right now; meaningful while
`status = "running"`.

retryable.description:
True for terminal non-success states a re-`POST /v1/deps/apply` can
retry (the apply is idempotent over already-installed deps).

DepsApplyRunJson.description:
One `deps_apply_runs` row for the polling surface. `running` rows are
reconciled against process liveness before serialization, so a crashed
apply reads as `failed` + `retryable` here rather than `running` forever.

version.description:
Running three-part base version. Not a capability signal: a nightly's
fourth component lives only in the git tag, so builds with and without
a feature report the same version. Test `features` membership instead.

features.description:
Advertised capability names, currently `network-provider-workload-env`,
`agent-test-json`, and `managed-credential-base-url`. The list grows
over time; an absent or empty list means none are present.

level.description:
Conventionally `info`, `warn`, `error`, or `debug`. Open set: the event
writer accepts any label.

kind.description:
Dotted namespace (e.g. `command.started`). Open set; filterable by
exact match, or by prefix when the filter ends in `.`.

source.description:
Conventionally `system`, `api`, `acp`, `command`, `permission`, `cli`,
or `local`. Open set: nothing enforces the named constants.

connections_opened.description:
All three fields are `null` together when the window contains no
`ws.client_connected` and no `ws.client_disconnected` rows; otherwise
`connections_opened` and `connections_closed` are numbers (possibly
`0`), while `average_duration_ms` stays `null` until some disconnect
in the window carried a `duration_ms`. Unlike
`api_connections.request_count`, a fully quiet window is reported as
`null`, not `0`.

source.description:
`"provider_catalog"` when `models` comes from the provider's live
model listing; `"acp_advertised"` when it comes from the agent's
ACP `session/new` config options.

modes.description:
ACP-advertised `mode` values. Empty when the agent does not
expose a mode option (or, on the catalog fallback path, when ACP
discovery failed).

efforts.description:
ACP-advertised reasoning-effort values (the `thought_level`
session config option). Empty when the agent does not expose an
effort option (or, on the catalog fallback path, when ACP
discovery failed).

catalog_error.description:
Set when the provider declares a model listing endpoint but the
catalog is unavailable (fetch failed and no cache).

PermissionRequestView.description:
Public view of a permission request, suitable for the HTTP API. The
`detail` field is the parsed JSON of the durable `detail_json` column.

ok.description:
Orthogonal to `status`: `ok` is false when any finding was emitted,
`status` is `failed` only on a critical one. A warnings-only run is
`status: "succeeded"` with `ok: false`.

details.description:
Optional structured payload attached to the finding. `message` is the
human-readable summary; `details` carries the same facts in machine-
readable form so the history view, future dashboards, or downstream
observability can aggregate without parsing the message string.

remediation.description:
Operator-actionable remediation hint. `message` describes *what* is
wrong; `remediation` describes *how to fix it*. Kept as a separate
field so CLI/UI surfaces can render it distinct from the diagnostic
text and so callers can lint findings for "must have a hint".

next_cursor.description:
Always emitted; `null` on the final page. Matches the `/v1/logs/*`
cursor shape so a client can page every list surface the same way.

ok.description:
Orthogonal to `status`: `ok` is false when any finding was emitted,
`status` is `failed` only on a critical one. A warnings-only run is
`status: "succeeded"` with `ok: false`.

oneOf.description: Reading files or data.
Modifying files or content.
Removing files or data.
Moving or renaming files.
Searching for information.
Running commands or code.
Internal reasoning or planning.
Retrieving external data.
Switching the current session mode.
Other tool types (default).

ToolKind.description:
Categories of tools that can be invoked.

Tool kinds help clients choose appropriate icons and optimize how they
display tool execution progress.

See protocol docs: [Creating](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/tool-calls#creating)

oneOf.description:
The tool call hasn't started running yet because the input is either
streaming or we're awaiting approval.
The tool call is currently running.
The tool call completed successfully.
The tool call failed with an error.

ToolCallStatus.description:
Execution status of a tool call.

Tool calls progress through different statuses during their lifecycle.

See protocol docs: [Status](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/tool-calls#status)

oldText.description: Deliberately serialized as `null` for creates instead of omitted.

oneOf.description:
`oldText`, `newText`, and `_meta` mirror ACP's `ToolCallContent::Diff`
wire shape verbatim; the camelCase spelling is intentional fidelity to
the protocol, not drift from this API's snake_case convention.

CapturedMeta.description: ACP `_meta` passed through unmodified; the shape is the agent's, not ours.

advertised.description:
Whether the command matched the agent's last advertised list. `false`
means the agent may ignore or misinterpret the invocation; omitted
when no list has ever been advertised. Advisory only — the prompt is
submitted regardless, because agents accept unadvertised commands and
the stored list can be stale.

available_commands.description:
Slash commands the agent last advertised for this session via ACP
`available_commands_update` (latest-wins). Empty when nothing has been
advertised; may be stale until the agent re-advertises.

updated_at.description:
When the stored list was last replaced. `null` when no list has ever
been advertised.

AvailableCommandResponse.description:
Wire shape of one agent-advertised slash command (compact projection of
the ACP `AvailableCommand`; names carry no leading slash).

config_options.description:
The session's config options as last observed: seeded from
`session/new` at create, refreshed by `session/set_config_option`
responses and `config_option_update` notifications. Empty when no
snapshot has been stored (sessions created before the feature).

updated_at.description: When the stored snapshot was last replaced. `null` when none exists.

ignored.description:
Configured features (mode, model) the agent's advertised capabilities
could not honor; the session proceeded on agent defaults. Omitted when
nothing was ignored, so list/read responses are unchanged.

feature.description:
What kind of configured feature was ignored: `mcp.server`,
`agent.mode`, `agent.model`, `agent.effort`, or `agent.config_option`.

value.description:
The configured value that was dropped: the MCP server name, or the
mode/model/effort/config-option value.

capability.description:
The capability the agent would have had to advertise
(`mcpCapabilities.*`), or — for `agent.mode`/`agent.model`/
`agent.effort`/`agent.config_option` — the `session/new` config
option that would have had to carry the value
(`sessionConfig.configOption` for map entries).

option_id.description:
The `[agent.config_options]` id the record is about. Present only for
`agent.config_option` features, where `feature` alone cannot name the
dropped option.

IgnoredFeature.description:
A configured feature the runtime routes around because the agent does not
advertise the capability backing it. The feature stays in config; this
record surfaces the omission through init reports and session events.

available_commands.description:
Slash commands the agent last advertised for this session via ACP
`available_commands_update` (latest-wins). Empty when nothing has been
advertised; may be stale until the agent re-advertises.

state.description:
Derived per request from the durable row plus in-flight prompt and
permission state; a wider set than the durable `status`.

sources.description: Total configured user sources after the add.

catalog.description: True for the curated catalog; false for user/ad-hoc sources.

SkillMetadata.description:
One installable skill surfaced by `source get` inspection: the selector to
pass to `add`, plus the frontmatter identity read from its `SKILL.md`.

sources.description: Total configured user sources after the removal.

repo.description: `owner/repo`, the GitHub source of the skills.

catalog.description: True for the embedded curated catalog; false for user-declared sources.

skills.description:
Selectors accepted by `add` (indexed catalog sources only; empty for
user sources — use `source get` to enumerate those live).

essential.description: Subset of `skills` installed by the Standard Setup essentials step.

supported.description:
Whether the active agent is a managed Agent Skills install target.
When false, `skills` is always empty and `install_dir` is absent.

InstalledSkill.description:
One entry in the day-2 list surface. Unlike [`SkillInstallEntry`] it
carries provenance: the source id recorded in the managed marker at
install time, absent for skills the user placed in the install root by
hand (which `remove` will refuse to delete).

provider_error.description:
Populated when configured-provider resolution fails (missing/unselected
credential, corrupt secret). Carries a remote-safe message so the
monitoring endpoint stays reachable in exactly the broken state an
operator queries it to diagnose. `None` on the happy path.

deps_apply_in_flight.description:
True while any dependency apply is running install snippets —
a `POST /v1/deps/apply`, an `acps deps apply`, or a detached
background apply spawned by `acps init --deps-apply-async` — derived
from the live `deps_apply_runs` row (pid-checked) plus the daemon's
own apply lock. Poll `GET /v1/deps/apply/runs/latest` for run identity
and progress. Advisory: a caller about to restart or reconfigure the
runtime should wait for it to clear; the apply itself survives a
daemon restart (install children run in their own sessions).

client_ip.description:
Redacted to `null` whenever a `RequestOrigin` is serialized into an API
response; only persisted event payloads carry the resolved address.

status.description:
Always `running`: the session is published only after it is created in
that state, so no other value is observable here.

Session status after the request was applied. `cancelled`, `closed`, and
`errored` are terminal, as is `completed_awaiting_ack` until the result
is acknowledged.

Current session status. `waiting_for_input` is the steady state while a
prompt is pending; `cancelled`, `closed`, and `errored` are terminal, as
is `completed_awaiting_ack` until the result is acknowledged.

signals.description:
The full ordered signal stream, identical to the `signals` field of
`hello`, so a REST poller and a socket client fold the same input into
the same category view.

kind.description:
Machine-readable prompt identity, from `HostedPromptKind::as_str`. Field
order here is the wire order; `kind` sits beside `request_id` so a
client can route on it before parsing the rest.

style.description:
Rendering hint. Unlike `kind`, this set is closed: a client may switch
on it exhaustively.

value.description:
Stable option id an answer may address by `{"value": "<id>"}`; unlike
`label` it survives display rewording.

InputAcceptedResponse.description:
REST twin of the `input_accepted` server event: the socket carries the ack
as an event frame, `POST /v1/init/sessions/{id}/input` returns it as the
success data.

DepositCredentialResponse.description:
`POST /v1/init/credential` result: the flat secrets persisted plus the
managed apply outcome, mirroring the admin-tier apply response.

config_version.description:
Config schema version. `1` is the only supported value; every other
value is rejected at load.

extensions.description:
Operator-declared extension instances, keyed by operator-chosen name.
See [`ExtensionConfig`].

mode.description:
Tunnel provisioning mode: `"generated"` or `"managed"`. Validated only
when `enabled = true`; any string is accepted while disabled.

exposure.description:
Public exposure method. `"tunnel"` is the only accepted value. Validated
only when `enabled = true`; any string is accepted while disabled.

cloudflared_deployment.description:
Where `cloudflared` runs: `"host"` (default), `"docker"`, or
`"external"`. Validated only when `enabled = true`; any string is
accepted while disabled.

sandbox.description:
Isolation backend that the agent harness and mediated shells run inside.
Default `off` preserves single-process behavior; other modes wrap each
spawn so the workload cannot read the daemon's secrets/state or reach its
control socket. See [`SandboxConfig`].

SandboxConfig.description:
Selects how the agent harness and mediated shells are isolated from the
daemon. The daemon always derives the set of its own sensitive paths to mask
(config dir, state dir) from its path helpers, so an operator cannot forget
to protect them; the fields below only add to or parameterize that.

wrapper.description:
Wrapper argv for `mode = "custom"`: prepended to the harness command
(e.g. `["systemd-run", "--scope", "-p", "..."]`). Required for `custom`,
ignored otherwise.

mask_paths.description: Extra absolute paths to mask (read-deny) on top of the daemon's own.

allow_paths.description:
Extra absolute paths the workload may read+write (e.g. bwrap binds)
beyond the workspace root.

CodeSourceConfig.description:
Source for code that init should seed under `<workspace.root>/usr/code/`.

The only `type` value today is `git`. The schema is shaped as an enum so
that additional code-source kinds can be added without invalidating
existing configs, but loaders reject unknown values fail-fast.

name.description:
Override the derived `<repo-name>` directory under
`<workspace.root>/usr/code/`. Defaults to the trailing path segment of
the repository URL with any `.git` suffix stripped.

level.description:
Conventional tracing level name: `"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`,
`"debug"`, or `"trace"`. Not validated, and not currently read by the
runtime, which logs at `warn`.

local_retention_days.description:
Retention window in days for local log records. Not currently read by
the runtime.

effort.description:
ACP-advertised reasoning-effort value (the agent's `thought_level`
session config option), applied on session creation like `mode`.

config_options.description:
Generic ACP session config options (option id → value), applied on
session creation after the typed mode/model/effort lanes. Ids the
typed lanes own are rejected at validation; entries the agent does
not advertise are reported as ignored features, never errors.

harness_version.description:
Pin the harness to a specific GitHub Release tag (e.g. `"v0.42.0"`).
Consulted by both install and managed update when the harness install
path is `github_release`; updates target the pin instead of the latest
release. Default (None) resolves the latest release.

adapter_override.description:
Operator-designated ACP adapter for a registry agent: the agent is
launched through this adapter binary while the registry harness and
every other registry-derived behavior stay managed. Mutually exclusive
with the `[agent.install]` escape hatch.

AgentConfigOptionValue.description:
One `[agent.config_options]` value. `Bool` must stay first in the untagged
order so TOML `true` never parses as the string `"true"` — a select option
may legitimately advertise the ValueId `"true"`, and only the TOML type
distinguishes the two.

AgentAdapterOverrideConfig.description:
Operator-designated ACP adapter for a registry agent. Mirrors the registry
`[agents.adapter]` spec shape but round-trips through the operator config:
the registry spec types are catalog-shaped and Deserialize-only, so they
cannot appear in the published config schema. `command` doubles as the
adapter identity (the registry `AdapterSpec.id`), which keeps the launch
command and the updater's native probe target from diverging.

github.description:
GitHub repo as `owner/repo` or a `https://github.com/` URL. Required
when `install.github` is used; otherwise informational (surfaced as
the adapter's source URL).

shell_rerun.description:
Update the adapter by re-running the shell install recipe. Without it a
shell-only override is skipped by managed update.

AgentInstallConfig.description:
Operator-facing escape hatch for installing an agent whose entry is not
in the embedded registry (private fork, unreleased build, custom adapter).
The runtime resolves registry-listed agents from `data/agents.toml`
keyed off `[agent].id`; this struct is consulted only when the operator
explicitly writes `[agent.install]` to override that resolution.

type.description: Install mechanism. `"shell"` is the only operator-facing value.

targets.description:
At least one target. Every load path that reads an `[array]` block
rejects an empty list; `primary_target` must name one of these ids.

timeout_action.description:
Action when a pending permission request expires. Absent leaves the
`"deny"` default.

PermissionTimeoutAction.description: Expiry action for a pending permission request.

PromptsConfig.description:
Configuration for the stale-prompt sweeper background task. When no
ACP `session/update` notification has touched a `pending`/`running`
prompt row for `stale_threshold`, the sweeper flips it to terminal
`Stalled` so polling clients always see the row settle. The sweep
runs every `sweep_interval` from `acps serve`.

install.description:
Optional install action for `acps deps apply`. When absent, the
command is "check-only" and `acps deps apply` will report it as
not actionable rather than guessing a package manager. This
keeps Dependency Apply narrowly scoped per the Phase 4 spec:
no cross-distro reconciliation, no auto-derived package names —
the operator declares each install action explicitly.
Only valid under `[[dependencies.commands]]`; declaring it under
`packages`, `runtimes`, or `mcp` fails config load.

DependencyInstallAction.description:
Operator-declared install action for one dependency. Intentionally
minimal: a single shell snippet, an optional `creates` postcheck,
and a scope marker that distinguishes "runs as the runtime user"
from "needs OS-wide privilege" so the apply runner knows when to
escalate — and never silently downgrades privileged work to user
scope behind the operator's back.

shell.description:
Shell snippet executed via `[workspace].default_shell -c`.
Operator declares it verbatim — no apt/brew/yum derivation in
the runtime.

creates.description:
PATH name that must resolve to an executable after `shell`
completes. Defaults to the dependency entry's `name`. The apply
runner records `available = true` only when this resolves
post-install.

scope.description:
`user` (default) runs as the runtime user; `system` declares
the action needs OS-wide privilege (typically sudo). The
runner emits a clear distinction in the audit log and a
confirmation prompt for `system` scope so operators don't
invoke `apt-get install` from a stale CLI invocation.

timeout_secs.description:
Optional timeout override in seconds. Defaults to 600s
(10 minutes) — same cap as the agent installer. Bounded above at
validation by `MAX_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (86400, 24 hours); `0` is
rejected, so omit the field rather than zeroing it.

oneOf.description:
Runs as the runtime user. No privilege escalation. Suitable
for npm globals under `~/.local/`, language toolchains in
$HOME, etc.

Action needs OS-wide privilege (system package manager, writes
under /usr or /opt). Runs directly when the process is root,
escalates through passwordless `sudo -n` when it isn't (never a
password prompt), and otherwise refuses early with a clear
"privilege required" outcome — the runner never falls back to
user scope.

HttpHeaderRef.description:
One MCP HTTP header, valued either by a whole-value secret ref
(`value_ref`) or by a `${NAME}`-interpolated template (`value`).
Exactly-one is enforced in validation rather than serde so TOML errors
stay readable; `source()` is the runtime accessor that upholds it.

SkillsConfig.description:
User-declared Agent Skills sources (managed via `acps skills source add`),
layered alongside the embedded curated catalog. Unlike the catalog these
are operator-supplied and untrusted by default.

alias.description: Unique alias used by `acps skills add <alias> ...` and `source get`.

trusted.description:
Operator assertion that the source has been vetted. Defaults false;
installs from untrusted sources are allowed but surfaced as such.

socket_path.description:
Override path for the internal local Unix-domain socket. When unset the
daemon binds `~/.local/share/acp-stack/acps-local.sock`. Override is
intended for integration tests; deployed instances should leave it
unset.

session_auth.description:
Controls whether local Unix-socket session-tier HTTP routes require an
explicit session key. Public HTTP tiering is unaffected.

ExtensionConfig.description:
A typed, data-declared extension seam. An `[extensions.<name>]` table
declares one instance of an acp-stack-defined extension type; acp-stack
supervises or serves the type's generic contract and never learns the
extension's semantics. The struct is flat across all types; the extensions
validator rejects fields that do not belong to the declared `type`.

provider.description:
`network-provider` only. Lifecycle provider argv, invoked as
`<exe> setup|teardown <args...>` around each network-isolated spawn.
Empty means no provider: the namespace stays deny-all.

provider_timeout.description:
`network-provider` only. Duration string applied independently to
provider setup and teardown.

provider_stderr.description:
`network-provider` only. Where provider stderr goes: the daemon's
stderr diagnostic channel, or discarded. Stdout is always discarded.

workload_env.description:
`network-provider` only. Environment variables injected into every
workload spawned inside the provider's namespace (agent harness,
mediated commands, ACP terminals) so the workload can reach whatever
egress path the provider set up — proxy endpoints, CA bundle paths.
Never passed to the provider executable itself, and never in argv.
`BTreeMap` for deterministic ordering across serialization round-trips.

capability.description:
`managed-state` only. The state contract the namespace applies;
`provider-credential` is the only capability today.

ExtensionType.description:
The extension types acp-stack defines. Declaring a `network-provider`
instance switches every sandboxed spawn to an isolated network namespace
whose policy belongs to the external provider executable; declaring a
`managed-state` instance grants an external orchestrator ownership of a
named state namespace via the admin apply endpoint.
